name: Amarnath Shakti Peetha
summary: Amarnath Shakti Peetha is counted among the 51 Shakti Peethas. Tradition associates this seat with the Throat (tradition varies) of Sati.

mythologySignificance:
In Shakti Peetha pilgrimage enumerations, Amarnath is remembered as a Himalayan seat linked to the Sati–Shakti narrative (throat association in some lists; traditions vary). The same mountain landscape is famous for the ice lingam of Shiva — so peetha devotion and Amar Katha Shaiva lore meet in one high-altitude kshetra.

Pilgrimage literature treats Amarnath Shakti Peetha as a tirtha — a crossing where devotion to Goddess Mahamaya tradition is believed to bear fruit more readily than in ordinary space. Accounts summarised here follow widely cited epic, Puranic, and regional mahatmya traditions; temple priests remain the guides for ritual detail.
localBeliefs:
Pilgrims on the Amarnath Yatra often hold both Shiva’s ice lingam and the Goddess’s peetha association in mind. Seasonal access, registered yatra rules, and weather windows structure safe devotion.

Local tellings differ on the exact peetha detail; yatra priests and Kashmir pilgrimage lore remain the practical guides on the ground.
